evals.prompt: Harborline DevSummit is on 14 November and we finally have four sponsors signed. Verilume Systems took Platinum at $14,000 and paid on 2 October. Klarstack took Gold at $6,000, invoice went out 9 October, nothing received. Nordpath Analytics also took Gold at $6,000 and wired half of it last week, said the rest comes when their PO clears. Bitmoor took Silver at $2,000, paid. I want to get moving tonight: put all four logos up on the website, send everyone a welcome pack. For the perk lists I'll just copy what's in our prospectus PDF since that's what they bought anyway. Can you set me up with a tracker and the welcome emails?
evals.expected_output: A tier-by-perk fulfillment matrix built from the four signed agreements with per-cell states, a payment gate that releases Verilume and Bitmoor while holding Klarstack and Nordpath, communicated holds via a named liaison, and a refusal to derive the perk list from the prospectus.
expectations: Builds a tier-by-perk matrix with perks as rows and tiers or sponsors as columns, not a single flat list of perks
Gives each matrix cell a state along a promised, scheduled, delivered, evidenced progression
States the promise column quotes each signed agreement, and declines to build the perk list from the prospectus PDF
Explains that the prospectus is the sales document while custom-negotiated deltas exist only in the signed contract
Holds every Klarstack perk, including the website logo, until the invoice is paid in full
Treats Nordpath Analytics's half payment as not-paid-in-full and holds their perks too
Releases perks for Verilume Systems and Bitmoor, whose payments are confirmed
Communicates each hold to the affected sponsor through their liaison, naming what is queued and why
Rejects letting an unpaid sponsor discover the hold at the venue door or at setup time
Names one liaison per sponsor
Asks for the hard pre-event deadlines (printer dates, program lock, newsletter schedule) rather than sequencing work from the 14 November event date

evals.prompt: Ten weeks until Brackenmoor Tech Days. Our lanyard printer wants final artwork in six days or we lose the slot, the swag bag print run closes in three weeks, the printed program locks five weeks out, and our newsletter goes out every Tuesday. Cindercloud bought the lanyard tier for $2,500 and their invoice is still open, no payment. Meanwhile Tesserly (Silver, paid) emailed asking if we can kick off with their social posts first since those are quick wins and we have plenty of time before the event. What order should I work through all this?
evals.expected_output: A delivery order sequenced by earliest hard deadline with printed surfaces ahead of digital ones, the printer date named as the fulfillment clock, Cindercloud's artwork still held behind payment with the deadline communicated to them, and a dated asset table.
expectations: Sequences perk delivery by earliest hard deadline first, not by ease of execution or by the event date
States the fulfillment clock starts at the printer's six-day date, not the ten-week event date
Places printed surfaces (lanyard, swag bag, signage) ahead of digital ones (newsletter, social, slides)
Declines to start with Tesserly's social posts on the grounds that they are quick
States a logo missed on a printed run is unfixable afterwards and becomes a make-good negotiation instead of a perk
Holds Cindercloud's lanyard artwork behind payment rather than sending it to the printer on an open invoice
Tells Cindercloud the print deadline explicitly so they can decide in time, instead of silently letting the slot lapse
Gives each asset a needed-by date tied to a named driver such as the printer date, program lock, or newsletter send
Sorts the deadline table by date and treats its top row as the clock
Shares the sponsor-facing part of the deadline table with each sponsor

evals.prompt: We run Tidewater Ops Meetup, all volunteers, about 220 people show up, and our own published sponsor rules say we do not share attendee contact details. Ferrolane signed at our top tier, $9,000, biggest cheque we have ever had. Their partner manager emailed: they want the attendee email list post-event, and if that is a problem they suggest we just add a little 'opt in to Ferrolane's newsletter' checkbox on the raffle entry form they are running at their booth. They also offered to bring their own badge scanners so we do not have to do anything. I really do not want to lose them. What can I actually offer?
evals.expected_output: A refusal of the attendee list, the newsletter checkbox and the badge scanners at a community-run event, with aggregate demographics offered as the default and a properly consented raffle as the higher-value option, including its consent statement, single-sponsor hand-off and deletion step.
expectations: Refuses the bulk attendee list outright rather than parking it as a last-resort or lower-priority option
Refuses sponsor badge scanning at this community-run event
States the refusal holds even for the largest sponsor, whose choice is the remaining options or no deal
Identifies the newsletter opt-in checkbox on the raffle form as the banned bulk-capture move in disguise, not a middle ground
Offers aggregate demographics (role mix, seniority mix, company-size mix, no names) as the default answer
Offers a consented opt-in raffle as the higher-value option where that perk was sold
States plainly at the point of entry what is collected and that it goes to Ferrolane specifically
Hands the raffle entries to Ferrolane only
Deletes the organizer's own copy of the entries after hand-off
States the entries never merge into any organizer list and the raffle never substitutes for an attendee list
Briefs the volunteers that the raffle and the aggregate demographics document are the only data hand-offs that exist
Notes the raffle carries a compliance cost the aggregate document does not, and that a mishandled hand-off cannot be walked back

evals.prompt: Ridgewire Conf wrapped Saturday, 310 attendees, four sponsors. Auxograph was our headline sponsor at $12,000 and on the exploratory call back in June they told us straight out that success for them was five qualified hiring conversations. Here is what we have for them: their booth raffle collected 34 entries, their two booth staff logged 12 conversations in their notebook, and their job post on our site got 61 views. We also completely forgot to put their logo on the rotating break slides, nobody noticed until I was going through my notes yesterday. Our marketing volunteer drafted something that opens with '500,000+ brand impressions across the weekend' and closes asking them to commit to the same tier for next year. She wants to polish it over the next few weeks. Thoughts before I send?
evals.expected_output: A report sent inside 72 hours, scored against Auxograph's own five-hiring-conversations metric, carrying the real small numbers with interpretation labels, self-disclosing the missed break-slide logo with a make-good, dropping the invented impressions figure and the hard renewal ask, and closing with a renew/renegotiate/drop read handed to the outreach motion.
expectations: Sends the report within 72 hours of the event rather than polishing it over the following weeks
Scores Auxograph's outcomes against their own stated metric of five qualified hiring conversations, not a generic one
Reports the real figures (34 raffle entries, 12 booth conversations, 61 job-post views) rather than inflating or omitting them for being small
Rejects the '500,000+ brand impressions' line as an invented, unmeasurable reach number
States that an invented reach number damages the credibility of the real numbers printed beside it
Labels what each number does and does not show, for example that raffle entries show booth draw rather than lead quality
Names the missed break-slide logo in the report itself, before Auxograph discovers it
Attaches a make-good to the slipped break-slide perk
Includes a delivered-versus-promised table with per-perk evidence such as a photo, link or screenshot
Includes aggregate audience data (attendance, role, seniority, company-size mix) and no attendee names
Removes the hard renewal ask from the close, leaving next edition as dates and a light note
Produces a renew, renegotiate or drop read on Auxograph and hands it with the report to the sponsor outreach motion
Does not build a renewal follow-up cadence or sequence inside this work

evals.prompt: Quillbase is sponsoring our hackathon (Friday evening through Sunday afternoon) at $7,500. Their package includes a 45-minute sponsored workshop slot plus $2,000 of API credits they are giving to the teams. Their marketing lead came back with: they would like the slot on Sunday because that is when their people are free-ish, their team is fully remote so instead of sending anyone they will give us a really thorough PDF walkthrough for participants, and the proposed title is 'Getting production-ready with Quillbase'. Honestly their brand is a perfect fit for our crowd and the topic sounds right, so I was going to just say yes to all of it. Anything I should push back on?
evals.expected_output: A hard requirement for a named on-site representative for the credits perk (with an independent-user fallback), a content review of the sponsored slot rather than brand-fit approval, the workshop moved off the final day, and staffing guidance passed to the sponsor.
expectations: Makes a named on-site representative a hard condition of the API-credits perk rather than a nice-to-have
Rejects the PDF walkthrough as a substitute for a live person when participants hit friction under time pressure
States that a tool with nobody available to troubleshoot it gets abandoned the moment it stops working
Offers an enthusiastic independent user of the tool as the on-site point of contact when no company representative can attend
Reviews the actual content of the sponsored slot before confirming it, not just the sponsor's brand and topic
Flags that a 'getting production-ready' session asking a time-boxed hackathon audience to invest hours works against the event's own format
Refuses to confirm the sponsored session on brand or logo fit alone
Moves the workshop off Sunday to the Friday or Saturday of the event
Passes along guidance to send someone who can tell the company's story and participate with the community rather than a sales representative
Collects the workshop title, abstract and speaker name as intake assets against a deadline

evals.prompt: Steelharbor Dev Days has nine sponsors signed this year, up from four. There are two of us organizing and realistically we each have about four hours a week for this. Mix is: Marrowgate took Platinum and it is their first time sponsoring anything of ours, Pellucid Labs has sponsored all four editions and already told me they are in for next year too, and the other seven are small Silvers who have all done it before and know the drill. My plan was to book a 45-minute kickoff call with each of the nine so nothing falls through the cracks. Sound right?
evals.expected_output: An onboarding menu ranked by value per unit of effort, checklist emails as the default for the repeat Silvers, kickoff calls promoted only for Marrowgate and Pellucid Labs with the condition named, and an intake form recommended at this roster size.
expectations: Ranks the onboarding options explicitly by value returned per unit of effort rather than by which is cheapest
Names the checklist email as the default instrument for the bulk of the roster
Declines the plan of booking a kickoff call with all nine sponsors
Promotes a kickoff call for Marrowgate as a top-tier, first-time sponsor and names that as the promotion condition
Promotes a kickoff call for Pellucid Labs as a compounding multi-edition relationship and names that as the promotion condition
Recommends an intake form at nine sponsors, citing roughly three sponsors as the point where it repays its setup cost
Generates each welcome email from that sponsor's own column of the fulfillment matrix
Writes the welcome email against specific named program moments the sponsor's team can put in a calendar, not a flat benefits list
Keeps the accompanying asset kit deliberately minimal (photos, a presentation template, one contact-request email) rather than a sprawling toolkit
States the ranking is a default that the four-hours-a-week effort ceiling and the compounding relationship re-rank

evals.prompt: Our published prospectus for Calderwood Summit says Gold is capped at three sponsors and lanyard branding is exclusive to the Lanyard tier. We have all three Golds signed. Now Ombrelle Data has come in wanting Gold too, at full price, and separately our Platinum sponsor Harkwood asked whether their logo could also go on the lanyard since they are paying nearly double everyone else. We are about $11,000 behind on sponsorship revenue for this edition. Realistically nobody reads the caps page of the prospectus. Can I make both of these work?
evals.expected_output: A refusal of both the fourth Gold and the shared lanyard surface, grounded in the published caps the matrix must honor, with a non-breaching alternative offered instead of a quiet oversell.
expectations: Refuses to sell a fourth Gold against a published cap of three
Refuses to add Harkwood's logo to the lanyard, which was sold as the Lanyard tier's exclusive surface
States the fulfillment matrix must honor every published cap, covering exclusive surfaces, premium placements and pitch slots
Describes an oversold exclusive surface as one promise two sponsors hold at the same time
States that delivering an oversold exclusive to one sponsor breaks it for the other in public
Rejects 'nobody reads the caps' as a reason to breach one
Offers a route that does not breach the published inventory, such as a non-exclusive surface, an add-on, or first pick at the next edition
Declines to treat the $11,000 revenue shortfall as grounds to override published inventory

evals.prompt: Nine days out from Alderfen Conf and three different sponsors have emailed this week asking basically the same things: when can they get in to set up, how do they ship their boxes to the venue, and is there power at the tables. I was going to write one FAQ page on our website and just reply to all of them with the link so I stop answering the same email. We already did the whole expo floor layout a few weeks back, tier specs, setup schedule, all of that. Is the FAQ page enough?
evals.expected_output: An answered logistics FAQ pushed to sponsors before they ask, direct organizer contact scheduled for the venue-specific items, a per-sponsor day-of brief a week out, and a doors-open booth walk photographing placements as matrix evidence.
expectations: Sends each sponsor an already-answered logistics FAQ rather than waiting for them to ask
Covers the setup and teardown window, shipping to the venue, whom to send, electricity, WiFi and additional A/V equipment
Rejects a self-service FAQ page as sufficient because shipping, power and A/V are venue-specific and route to direct organizer contact
Puts a logistics call or thread with each sponsor's on-site lead on the fulfillment calendar
Produces one day-of brief per sponsor about a week out, carrying booth location and size, staff badge count and pickup, scheduled slots, an on-site organizer phone contact and teardown rules
Takes the booth specs and setup schedule from the existing floor layout work instead of re-deriving or restating them
Walks the booths at doors-open with the matrix in hand, photographing premium placements, banners and signage as cell evidence
